items.summary: Revocations targeted foreign nationals who allegedly broke terms of their visas, government says The US Department of State has canceled more than 175,000 visas since Donald Trump returned to office, quadrupling the pace of revocations under Joe Biden’s final year in the White House, according to a new tally released by the department this week. The announcement said the revocations targeted foreign nationals who allegedly broke the terms of their visas, committed crimes, called for violence against Americans, defrauded US citizens, abused the immigration system or endangered national security. Many followed run-ins with law enforcement, the department said, with assault, drunk driving, theft and drug offenses the leading causes, alongside reckless driving, sexual assault, child abuse and fraud. articles.title: SMTR25 다니엘, 데뷔 전부터 거대한 생일 잔치…룩스 주인공
articles.snippet: SMTR25 다니엘(이다니엘)이 정식 데뷔 전부터 거대한 생일 선물을 받았다. 다니엘의 중국 팬덤은 8월11일 다니엘의 생일을 맞이해 대규모 응원 프로젝트를 진행했다. 특히 오늘(8월11일) 서울 광화문 동아미디어센터 외벽에 설치된 ‘룩스(LUUX)’ 전광판에선 다니엘의 영상이 송출 중이다. 다니엘은 SM엔터테인먼트 소속 공개 남자 연습생 팀인 SMTR25의 멤버로 아직 정식 데뷔를 하지 않은 상태. 데뷔 전부터 대규모 이벤트를 하는 건 다니엘 팬덤의 강력한 결집력을 보여주는 사례다.동아미디어센터 외벽에 있는 ‘룩스(LUUX)’는 국내 최대 규모 옥외 LED 대형 스크린으로 총 면적이 축구장 절반 크기인 3,000㎡에 달하고, 곡면과 정면이 결합된 구조로 몰입감을 선사한다. 서울의 랜드마크인 광화문에 위치해 높은 노출도와 화제성을 모두 갖추고 있다는 평가를 받는다.‘룩스’를 장식한 다니엘은 SMTR25 첫 팬미팅 투어를 통해 글로벌 팬들을 만나고 있다.전효진 기자 jhj@

articles.title: Probation officers vote for strike action after warning early releases will add to excessive workloads - as it happened
articles.snippet: Union chief says vote is about staff ‘warning they cannot protect the public properly’ In his pooled TV interview, Andy Burnham repeated the point he made in his Facebook post earlier (see 9.58am), saying he was confident that more could be done to free up space in the prison system (which would allow the early release system to be changed so that PC Andrew Harper’s killers are excluded). Burnham said that since becoming PM he had been pushing the system “every single day” to go further. Explaining how extra space could be found (see 9.19am), he particularly singled out the more than 2,000 prisoners on indeterminate IPP (imprisonment for public protection) sentences. He said: [The] plan will include issues like returning more foreign national offenders to their country of origin, and looking at the injustice of IPP sentences, which have led to young people, or young when they were imprisoned, being imprisoned indeterminately, and that clearly is unfair. My office was in touch with the family last night [see 10.04am], and I know the justice secretary is in regular touch as well. So, we will keep close to the family through this whole process because we understand how difficult this process has been for them. Continue reading...

articles.title: Feel the burn: why holidays from hell make for blistering fiction
articles.snippet: Family fallouts, failing marriages, sunburn, food poisoning ... from Deborah Levy’s hypnotic and disturbing Hot Milk to All In, Claire Powell’s all-inclusive nightmare, Leon Craig looks at the best novels about vile vacations Every summer, we long for a much-needed break from daily life, dreaming of self-reinvention in some distant paradise. But really, holidays can be absolute hell. Instead of relaxation we encounter heaving crowds, lumpy beds, the caprices of our loved ones and the grim truth that we can escape neither their worst failings nor our own, however far we travel. Small wonder, then, that the disaster holiday has become a booming subgenre in fiction. For most of us, the levels of luxury promised by hit TV series The White Lotus are pure fantasy, yet we’re all vulnerable to the expensive promises we’ve been sold. Two of the smartest offerings in fiction this summer come from Claire Powell’s All In and Chloë Ashby’s Family Friends. In the former, a struggling couple whose marriage is on the rocks go on an all-inclusive Spanish weekend break, paid for by a rich brother. Poignant and extremely funny, the frictions that ensue are all too believable. Continue reading...

articles.title: You Won’t Get Free of It by Rachel Aviv review – a subtle study of the mother-daughter bond
articles.snippet: The most complex of female relationships is thrown into sharp relief in this moving series of essays Rachel Aviv has a profound interest in the vagaries of human psychology: Strangers to Ourselves, her last book, profiled five people whose psychiatric states resisted straightforward explanation, testing the limits of the mental health system. A Pulitzer finalist, Aviv has become known for rigorous, penetrating journalism that is as empathic as it is insightful. Now comes You Won’t Get Free of It, six stories of mothers and daughters, all originally published in the New Yorker. Madness runs through this book, too, in the stories of Linda Bishop, a woman who, upon discharge from hospital after a psychotic break, holed up in an abandoned farmhouse and tried to subsist on apples alone, and of Mary, a woman whose delusions and paranoia were only seemingly cured as a side-effect of chemotherapy. It’s also there in the childhood memories of the psychologist Elizabeth Loftus – a professional court witness for those who have been accused of abuse, one of whom was Harvey Weinstein. Loftus’s mother was found drowned, perhaps as a result of suicide. In Aviv’s masterly profile, she teases out a conclusion that leaves you pondering the extent to which this memory expert can rely on her own recollections, and what that says about her particular line of work.
